title: Teaching in Schools of Acceptance of Diversity
what_it_is: Teaching in Schools of Acceptance of Diversity

sections.label: Social and emotional skills education
sections.summary: Schools develop students' social and emotional skills through role modelling and platforms like CCE, Social Studies, History, Values in Action and Co-Curricular Activities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Acting Minister for Education Schools))
sentences.text: Complementing our emphasis on values education, we also develop in our students social and emotional skills that will enable them to appreciate diversity, empathise with and demonstrate respect for others and build positive relationships with others.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Acting Minister for Education Schools))
sentences.text: To achieve this, educators role model the values and we provide students with varied learning experiences through platforms, such as Character and Citizenship Education (CCE) lessons, Social Studies and History lessons, Values in Action programmes and Co-Curricular Activities.

sections.label: Uncovering stereotypes and prejudices
sections.summary: Students learn to uncover and reshape stereotypes and prejudices, such as through lower Secondary History lessons on post-war Singapore riots.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Acting Minister for Education Schools))
sentences.text: Students are also taught skills to uncover stereotypes and prejudices they may have and re-shape them, and ways to demonstrate respectful behaviours.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Acting Minister for Education Schools))
sentences.text: For example, in the lower Secondary History curriculum, students learn about the riots in post-war Singapore and the importance of managing race, religion and socio-economic challenges with sensitivity.

sections.label: Racial Harmony Day commemoration
sections.summary: Students have commemorated Racial Harmony Day every year on 21 July since 1997 to mark the 1964 racial riots.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Acting Minister for Education Schools))
sentences.text: Students in schools have been commemorating Racial Harmony Day every year on 21 July since 1997 to mark the racial riots of 1964.

sections.label: Diversity events in tertiary institutions
sections.summary: Events like the Global Community Day in Polytechnics and SMU's Diversity and Inclusion Conference deepen students' ability to manage diversity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Acting Minister for Education Schools))
sentences.text: Beyond discussing issues pertaining to diversity through modules and electives, there are events and activities, such as the Global Community Day held across all Polytechnics, as well as SMU's annual Diversity and Inclusion Conference, which deepen our students' ability to manage diversity.

sections.label: Improving CCE and Values in Action
sections.summary: The speaker says more such programmes could run under the PSD platform and will study the Member's suggestion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, run more of such programmes under the PSD platform.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We are always looking for ways to improve and ensure our CCE programmes and Values in Action programmes are relevant.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I will take the Member's suggestion on board and I will study it.
